prior_importants.description: The new rule for applying model groups ('one holding two or more `important` findings is applied only when they share a file and a line') checks file and line only. That is the very case the consolidator is told to keep apart ('Different defects at one line stay separate', review-consolidator.md L17), and it contradicts the mechanical rule this same commit adopts (`sameImportant`: same file, same start line, same normalized text). Trigger: on one line `exec(cmd)`, `security` reports command injection and `correctness` reports that the unhandled rejection is reported as success. Haiku groups them as one fix site. The orchestrator's check passes (same file, same line), so it applies the group, and the merge rules keep one description. The other `important` is never validated and never commented, which is the outcome the sentence says the rule prevents ('whether the model erred').

process_issues.description: This is round 4, so the importants-only budget applied. Only correctness and security were spawned (security because the delta changes the defense against instructions planted in finding text). conventions, docs, context and maintainability were skipped under the round budget. spec was skipped because there is no spec source.

Both reviewers noted that the §9 L178 wording for `merged_duplicates` ("the consolidator's `merged` count") can now differ from what §6 L127 says the orchestrator folds, since importants never fold. They did not re-raise it: it is covered by the merged_duplicates-wording minor posted in an earlier round, and round 4 owes no minors.
